programs.name: QuickSort
programs.description:
Sorts the list in place (Hoare partition), using three functions.

## quicksort(C)
1. Store the length: `n = len(C)`
2. Only if there is something to sort (`n > 1`):
  - choose the pivot with `choose_pivot(C)`
  - split C around the pivot with `partition(C, pivot)`, which gives the split index `p`
  - sort the front part `C[:p+1]` recursively and write it back into the same slice
  - sort the back part `C[p+1:]` recursively and write it back
3. Return `C` (outside the if, so short lists come back unchanged)

## choose_pivot(C)
1. Return the middle element: index `(len(C) - 1) // 2`

## partition(C, pivot)
1. Two pointers: `i` starts at the first index (0), `j` at the last (`len(C) - 1`)
2. Loop forever (`while True`):
  - move `i` right while `C[i] < pivot`
  - move `j` left while `C[j] > pivot`
  - if the pointers met or crossed (`i >= j`): return `j`
  - otherwise swap `C[i]` and `C[j]`
  - step both pointers inward: `i` up by 1, `j` down by 1

**Remember:** the split index `p` is the last index of the front part, which is why it is `C[:p+1]` and `C[p+1:]`.
